subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the SCAMPER idea-generation technique, what does the letter 'S' stand for?
options: Substitute
Sketch
Simplify
Standardise
questions.explain: SCAMPER stands for Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to another use, Eliminate and Reverse/Rearrange.

questions.q: What is a mood board?
options: A collection of images, colours, textures and materials that communicates a theme or aesthetic
A scaled working drawing showing exact dimensions
A chart listing manufacturing costs for a product
A timeline showing the stages of the design process
questions.explain: A mood board gathers visual references to establish the style, feel and direction of a design early in the process.

questions.q: Why is design fixation considered a problem during idea generation?
options: It causes a designer to focus on one early idea, limiting the range of alternatives explored
It makes CAD models render too slowly
It forces the use of only recycled materials
It prevents a product from being manufactured by CAM
questions.explain: Design fixation narrows creative thinking by anchoring the designer to a single concept, reducing innovation.

questions.q: What is biomimicry as a source of design inspiration?
options: Taking inspiration from nature and living systems to solve design problems
Copying a competitor's existing product exactly
Using only biodegradable materials in a product
Testing a product with a group of users
questions.explain: Biomimicry draws on structures, forms and processes found in nature to generate design solutions.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of brainstorming or mind-mapping at the start of designing?
options: To generate a wide quantity of ideas quickly without early judgement
To produce a final, dimensioned working drawing
To calculate the exact cost of the finished product
To select suppliers for mass production
questions.explain: Brainstorming and mind maps encourage the free flow of many ideas, deferring evaluation until later.

questions.q: A designer wants to systematically combine different options for a product's shape, material and handle type to create new possibilities. Which technique is most suitable?
options: A morphological analysis chart
An orthographic drawing
A photorealistic CAD render
A Gantt chart
questions.explain: A morphological analysis chart lists features and their options in columns so combinations can be systematically explored.

questions.q: How does user-centred design help generate more successful ideas?
options: It focuses idea generation on the needs, wants and abilities of the intended users
It removes the need to make any prototypes
It guarantees the cheapest possible materials are used
It replaces the need for sketching entirely
questions.explain: User-centred design keeps the end user's requirements central, producing ideas that better meet real needs.

questions.q: In an isometric drawing, at what angle to the horizontal are the receding (side) lines usually drawn?
options: 30 degrees
45 degrees
60 degrees
90 degrees
questions.explain: Isometric drawings use vertical lines for uprights and 30-degree lines for the receding edges, with no vanishing point.

questions.q: Which feature is characteristic of a perspective drawing?
options: Lines converge towards one or more vanishing points
All edges are drawn at exactly 30 degrees
The front face is always drawn as a true shape
Only two-dimensional flat views are shown
questions.explain: Perspective drawing uses vanishing points so that parallel lines converge, giving a realistic sense of depth.

questions.q: Why would a designer use an exploded view drawing?
options: To show how the separate parts of a product fit together and in what order they assemble
To display the product's colour scheme and branding
To calculate the strength of a material under load
To record the results of user testing
questions.explain: An exploded view separates components along common axes to clarify assembly and the relationship between parts.

questions.q: What does an orthographic projection show?
options: Separate flat 2D views such as the front, plan and side of an object
A single 3D view with realistic shading
A photographic image of the finished product
A mind map of possible design ideas
questions.explain: Orthographic projection presents multiple 2D views (front, plan and end elevation) to give accurate dimensioned information.

questions.q: What is an advantage of using oblique projection to sketch an object?
options: The front face is drawn as a true shape, making it quick and easy to construct
It automatically produces photorealistic renders
It requires no straight lines at all
It shows the internal electronic circuit
questions.explain: In oblique projection the front face is drawn flat and true, with depth lines added at 45 degrees, making it simple to draw.

questions.q: A student wants to quickly communicate a 3D impression of a new pencil case idea, showing three faces without needing vanishing points. Which drawing method is most appropriate?
options: Isometric drawing
First-angle orthographic projection
A flow chart
A schematic circuit diagram
questions.explain: Isometric drawing gives a clear 3D impression of three faces using 30-degree lines and is quicker than full perspective.

questions.q: Before committing to manufacture, a designer wants to test the size, feel and ergonomics of a handheld controller. What should they make?
options: A physical prototype or model
A photorealistic 2D render only
A morphological analysis chart
A mood board
questions.explain: A physical prototype lets the designer test ergonomics, scale and function in three dimensions before manufacture.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation CAD stand for?
options: Computer Aided Design
Computer Assisted Drawing
Creative Art Design
Controlled Additive Deposition
questions.explain: CAD stands for Computer Aided Design, software used to create and edit 2D and 3D designs on a computer.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation CAM stand for?
options: Computer Aided Manufacture
Computer Assisted Modelling
Colour And Material
Central Assembly Method
questions.explain: CAM stands for Computer Aided Manufacture, where machines such as laser cutters or 3D printers make a product from CAD data.

questions.q: Which of the following is a genuine advantage of using CAD over hand drawing?
options: Designs can be easily edited, saved and shared, and viewed as accurate 3D models
It removes the need to consider the user's needs
It makes materials free to purchase
It guarantees no testing is ever required
questions.explain: CAD allows fast, accurate editing, storage, sharing and 3D visualisation, and links directly to CAM for manufacture.

questions.q: How does rapid prototyping using a 3D printer support the design process?
options: It quickly produces a physical model directly from a CAD file for testing and evaluation
It automatically writes the product specification
It replaces the need to generate any ideas
It selects the target market for a product
questions.explain: Rapid prototyping turns a CAD model into a physical object quickly, allowing designs to be tested and refined early.

questions.q: A design team in the UK needs colleagues in another country to view and comment on the exact same 3D model without posting physical drawings. Which approach best achieves this?
options: Sharing the CAD file electronically
Posting an isometric hand sketch
Emailing a mood board
Building a card model
questions.explain: CAD files can be shared instantly and globally, letting teams view, edit and comment on the same accurate model.

questions.q: Why do designers add annotation to their sketches and drawings?
options: To explain materials, dimensions, functions and construction details of the design
To make the drawing take longer to complete
To replace the need for any drawing at all
To hide information from the client
questions.explain: Annotation adds written notes to a drawing to communicate key design details clearly to others.
